title: QA follow-ups on the address-add handshake (four commits, three repos)
summary: A second wave of EUDPA-333 QA fixes, landed 21-23 September (after the alignment branch had already ported the ORIGINAL handshake feature once via s19's 16 September main-merge, 1446fcc/ea2bfe6/a3dcb6d). Four independent fixes: (1) ins 2b4be7c — validates tradeImportsAddressBookApi.baseUrl as a URL at startup (format: String → 'url') and sets Cache-Control: no-store on every add-address form render (GET and POST error paths) so a browser back-button never replays a stale/submitted form; (2) animals b7c5039b — the same URL-format hardening for tradeImportsAddressBookApi.baseUrl (tradeImportsInsFrontend.baseUrl was ALREADY 'url' on the branch via s24, for an unrelated reason) plus parametrising one party-picker unit test across all five party types instead of just consignor; (3) tests 48ea0c0 — extends the INS add-link E2E assertions (addresses-read-only.spec.ts) from consignor-only to all five party pickers; (4) tests cd378de — replaces the compose-only skipIfComposeEnvironment/skipUnlessComposeEnvironment gating with skipIfNonStubStackEnvironment/skipUnlessNonStubStackEnvironment (true whenever the stack runs outside stub mode — compose OR CDP) and rewrites fixtures/auth-state.ts's authCookieNameFor to derive INS's session-cookie name from the target baseURL's hostname (ins-sid on localhost/127.0.0.1/cdp-docker.test, sid elsewhere) instead of a static per-target cookieName field, so CDP minting no longer needs an extra config knob. Observable behaviour: address-book API misconfiguration now fails fast at boot instead of a mystery 500 later; the ins add-address form is never served from a cached/back-button state; the E2E suite proves the handshake link for every party, not just consignor, and gates correctly against a real CDP run instead of only the local compose stack.

ins: 2b4be7c fix(EUDPA-333): address QA AC gaps on INS add-address handshake (#34)
animals: b7c5039b fix(EUDPA-333): address QA AC gaps on INS handshake add link (#367)
tests: 48ea0c0 fix(EUDPA-333): extend handshake add-link E2E across all parties (#239)
cd378de fix(EUDPA-333): align INS handshake E2E gating with CDP behaviour (#233)

NOT in the tests repo's conflicts list, but the textual auto-merge is semantically broken — a landmine the conflict-marker scan misses entirely. main (cd378de) deletes the AuthTarget.cookieName? field, deletes the ins target's static cookieName: process.env.AUTH_SESSION_COOKIE_NAME ?? 'ins-sid' line, and rewrites authCookieNameFor(targetName) into authCookieNameFor(targetName, baseURL), which special-cases only targetName === 'ins' against a hostname allow-list. Independently, the branch's s24 stage added `cookieName: process.env.AUTH_SESSION_COOKIE_NAME ?? 'plants-sid'` to the `plants` target, using the OLD (pre-cd378de) AuthTarget.cookieName field and the OLD single-arg authCookieNameFor(targetName) it reads from. Because the two edits sit on non-overlapping lines (branch inside the `plants:` object literal, main inside the `ins:` object literal, the type declaration, and the function body), git's line-based 3-way merge auto-resolves with NO conflict markers — but the merged result sets `cookieName` on a `plants` object whose `AuthTarget` type no longer declares that field (a TypeScript compile error), and even if that were suppressed, main's rewritten authCookieNameFor never reads `AUTH_TARGETS[targetName]?.cookieName` any more, so plants' 'plants-sid' value becomes dead, unreachable configuration — plants would silently fall back to the generic AUTH_COOKIE_NAME ('sid') in the compose stack, exactly the animals-session-cookie collision s24 was built to prevent. Confirmed by reading the trial-merge tree content in full: the plants object literal at `d4ac0a8219760d380c137aeb19bf7b1492a5ab74:fixtures/auth-state.ts` still carries `cookieName: process.env.AUTH_SESSION_COOKIE_NAME ?? 'plants-sid'`, but the AuthTarget type two lines above it has already lost the `cookieName?: string;` field.

branchEquivalent.evidence: ins: `git grep -n 'no-store|Cache-Control' origin/feat/NO_JIRA-frontend-alignment -- src/` returns nothing; `tradeImportsAddressBookApi.baseUrl` is still `format: String` on the branch. animals: same format gap for the same key; the party-picker test is genuinely untouched by the branch (not partial-equivalent, simply unmodified since the merge base). tests: `skipIfNonStubStackEnvironment`/`skipUnlessNonStubStackEnvironment` do not exist anywhere on the branch; the branch's own fixtures/auth-state.ts change (s24) is unrelated in intent (giving plants a distinct dev cookie name) and predates cd378de's restructuring of the mechanism that would carry it.

verdictWhy: Every file except fixtures/auth-state.ts is a clean port (either take-branch-and-delete-resurrection, or a mechanical add of main's new format:'url'/no-store/test-parametrisation/skip-helper-rename behaviour). fixtures/auth-state.ts is a genuine decision: main's ins-only hostname-based cookie-name detection and the branch's static per-target cookieName field are two different designs for the same problem, and reconciling them (so plants keeps its distinct dev-mode session cookie AND main's CDP-aware ins detection survives) is a real judgement call, not a mechanical merge. Given the goal (main decides behaviour, the alignment ledger decides where code lives — but here main is also changing the MECHANISM, not just adding a value), the smallest change that preserves both behaviours is to generalise main's hostname-conditional branch from an if (targetName === 'ins') check into a small per-target compose-cookie-name lookup and delete the now-redundant AuthTarget.cookieName field entirely, matching D11's 'mirror the ins entry's shape exactly' instruction one level up (at the mechanism, not the field).

resolutions.take: Take main's authCookieNameFor(targetName, baseURL) mechanism and its AuthTarget type (drop cookieName? from the type). Generalise the single `if (targetName === 'ins')` hostname branch into a per-target compose-cookie-name lookup, e.g. `const COMPOSE_AUTH_COOKIE_NAMES: Record<string, string> = { ins: 'ins-sid', plants: 'plants-sid' }` consulted for any targetName present in it, instead of hardcoding 'ins' alone. Delete the branch's `cookieName: process.env.AUTH_SESSION_COOKIE_NAME ?? 'plants-sid'` line from the plants object literal (the field no longer exists on the type, and the lookup table now owns that value). Keep the `process.env.AUTH_SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` override as the first-priority check for both targets, per main's ordering.
resolutions.why: Preserves main's stated goal (derive the cookie name from where the stack is actually running, not a static per-target field, so CDP needs no extra config) while not silently regressing s24's plants-sid-on-compose behaviour, which the textual auto-merge would otherwise leave dead. This is the smallest change that keeps both intents: one function, one small lookup table, no new per-target config surface.

wireIn.what: The generalised COMPOSE_AUTH_COOKIE_NAMES lookup in fixtures/auth-state.ts must be consulted by authCookieNameFor for BOTH 'ins' and 'plants', not just 'ins' as main wrote it — main never needed a plants case because when cd378de landed, main's own AUTH_TARGETS had no plants cookieName entry at all.

behaviourChanges: ins: a malformed TRADE_IMPORTS_ADDRESS_BOOK_URL now fails config.validate({ allowed: 'strict' }) at process startup instead of surfacing later as an opaque fetch failure inside the address-book service client.

ins: every render of the add-address form (GET and every POST validation/API-error re-render) now carries Cache-Control: no-store, so a browser back button after a successful save, or after a validation error, never replays a stale form from cache.
animals: the same URL-format hardening applies to TRADE_IMPORTS_ADDRESS_BOOK_URL.

tests: the INS add-address handshake link is now asserted (present in non-stub mode, absent in stub mode) for all five party pickers (consignor, place of origin, consignee, importer, place of destination), not just consignor.

tests: the stub-vs-handshake-link E2E specs now gate correctly on CDP as well as the local compose stack (skipIfNonStubStackEnvironment/skipUnlessNonStubStackEnvironment), where before they gated on compose alone and would have behaved wrongly (or been silently skipped) against a real CDP run.

tests, once resolved per this cluster's decision: ins's session cookie name in E2E auth-state minting is derived from the target baseURL's hostname (ins-sid on localhost/127.0.0.1/cdp-docker.test, sid elsewhere) rather than a static config value, matching how the ins-frontend container actually names its cookie per environment; plants keeps its own distinct plants-sid on the same compose-hostname basis, which the textual auto-merge alone would have silently dropped.
knockOn: If fixtures/auth-state.ts's auto-merge is accepted as-is (without the resolution above), plants' E2E auth-state minting silently falls back to the generic 'sid' cookie on the compose stack, defeating the point of s24's plants-sid divergence and very likely re-introducing the animals/plants session collision on localhost that s24 exists to prevent — with no test failure calling it out, since nothing currently asserts the compose-stack cookie name per target directly (D-noted as an open question by s24 itself: 'the single AUTH_SESSION_COOKIE_NAME env var shared by the ins and plants entries').

openQuestions.question: Should the generalised compose-cookie-name lookup in fixtures/auth-state.ts (ins → ins-sid, plants → plants-sid) live in fixtures/auth-state.ts itself, or should it read the same per-service default convict already knows (auth.cookieName's isDevelopment ? '<service>-sid' : 'sid') so the two never drift? s24 already flagged the adjacent AUTH_SESSION_COOKIE_NAME single-env-var sharing as an open question it declined to redesign.
openQuestions.default: Keep it local to fixtures/auth-state.ts as a small static lookup table (as proposed in this cluster's resolution) — matching D11's 'mirror the ins entry's shape' instruction literally, and not reopening s24's explicitly parked redesign.

claims.statement: ins's fix sets Cache-Control: no-store on every add-address form render via a withNoStore wrapper, applied at four call sites (GET success, GET error, POST validation-error, POST API-error) but never on a redirect.
ins's fix converts tradeImportsAddressBookApi.baseUrl from format: String to format: 'url', so a malformed value now fails config.validate() at startup.
The branch has no Cache-Control handling anywhere in src/, confirmed by a full-tree grep against the branch HEAD.

main's fixtures/auth-state.ts rewrite deletes the AuthTarget.cookieName field and the ins target's static cookieName line, replacing them with authCookieNameFor(targetName, baseURL), which special-cases only targetName === 'ins'.
The branch's s24 stage independently added a static cookieName field to the plants AuthTarget entry, using the pre-cd378de shape.

The trial-merge tree's textual auto-merge of fixtures/auth-state.ts keeps the plants cookieName line while removing the field from the AuthTarget type and from authCookieNameFor's implementation — a broken combination with no conflict marker.
tests/e2e/features/auth.spec.ts is the tests repo's only listed conflict and is unrelated to either EUDPA-333 commit — neither 48ea0c0 nor cd378de touches it.
